notes_sections.title: Average Speed Concept
notes_sections.content:
Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Important: Do NOT take simple average of speeds unless time or distance conditions allow it.

Example:
A person travels 40 km/h for 2 hours and 60 km/h for 2 hours.
Total Distance = (40×2) + (60×2) = 80 + 120 = 200 km
Total Time = 4 hours
Average Speed = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 km/h.

notes_sections.title: Average Speed for Equal Distances
notes_sections.content:
If equal distances are covered at two different speeds,
Average Speed = (2xy) / (x + y)

Example:
Half distance at 30 km/h and half at 60 km/h.
Average Speed = (2×30×60)/(30+60) = 3600/90 = 40 km/h.

notes_sections.title: Relative Speed
notes_sections.content:
If two objects move towards each other,
Relative Speed = Sum of speeds.

If they move in same direction,
Relative Speed = Difference of speeds.

Example:
Two trains moving at 50 km/h and 70 km/h towards each other.
Relative Speed = 120 km/h.

notes_sections.title: Train Problems Basics
notes_sections.content:
If a train crosses a pole,
Distance = Length of train.

If a train crosses a platform,
Distance = Length of train + Length of platform.

Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

Example:
Train length = 200 m
Speed = 20 m/s
Time = 200 ÷ 20 = 10 seconds.

notes_sections.title: Speed and Time Inverse Relation
notes_sections.content:
When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

If speed increases in ratio a:b,
Time decreases in ratio b:a.

Example:
Speed ratio = 2:3
Time ratio = 3:2.

notes_sections.title: Unit Conversion
notes_sections.content:
To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

Example:
72 km/h × 5/18 = 20 m/s.

notes_sections.title: Common Mistakes
notes_sections.content:
1. Taking simple average instead of correct average speed.
2. Forgetting to add lengths in train problems.
3. Mixing km/h and m/s without conversion.
4. Adding speeds in same direction instead of subtracting.

notes_sections.title: Quick Summary
notes_sections.content:
Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.
For equal distance use (2xy)/(x+y).
Relative Speed depends on direction.
Always convert units properly.

tricks.title: Equal Distance Fast Formula
tricks.explanation: Use (2xy)/(x+y) directly when distances are equal.

tricks.title: Opposite Direction Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Add speeds when moving towards each other.

tricks.title: Same Direction Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Subtract speeds when moving in same direction.

tricks.title: Speed Ratio Trick
tricks.explanation: If speed ratio is known, invert it for time ratio (distance constant).

tricks.title: Train Pole Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Time to cross pole = Train length ÷ Speed.

tricks.title: Platform Crossing Trick
tricks.explanation: Add train and platform lengths before dividing by speed.
tricks.example: Train 150 m + Platform 100 m at 25 m/s → 250/25 = 10 seconds.
